intro.en: Aleph. The first letter, the number one, the breath before every word.
intro.src: The first of the three mother letters

lines.en: Look closely: an aleph is drawn from three letters. A yod above, a yod below, and a vav between them.
Yod, vav, yod: ten, six and ten make twenty-six, the number of God's four-letter Name. The Name is hidden inside the first letter.
The upper yod is the waters above, the lower yod the waters below, and the vav is the sky that holds them apart.
lines.src: Genesis 1:7, as the mystics read it

lines.en: Aleph makes no sound of its own. It is the open breath that every vowel rides on.
Aleph was made king over air: the sky in the world, the mild season in the year, the chest in the body.
Some sages taught that at Sinai the people heard only the first letter, the aleph of Anochi, "I am." A silence that held every word.
Echad, one, begins with aleph. In the Zohar God tells the aleph: my oneness will be known only through you.
Turn aleph around and read it backwards: אלף becomes פלא, pele. Wonder.
In the oldest Hebrew script aleph was drawn as an ox's head, horns and all. Alafim are oxen: the strength that pulls the plough.
The same three letters spell aluf, master; elef, a thousand; and a'alefcha, I will teach you.
Three mother letters: aleph, mem, shin. Air, water, fire. Aleph is the air between them, the tongue of the scale that keeps fire and water in balance.
Aleph is one. Spelled in full, אלף adds to 111: one, ten, a hundred. One at every level.
Every letter asked to begin the world. Aleph alone stood back and did not ask, and was promised the first word at Sinai instead.
